- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is low, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, reduce forecast for next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot; sentiment should be used to gauge whether correction is warranted.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true mean by >3% over 5+ days, apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1–2% from next forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast starts high and true outcome declines sharply, assume sentiment shift and adjust downward by 2–5% in next 5 days unless sentiment remains strong.  
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism but price declines, consider “sentiment lag” — forecast may be overreacting; reduce by 3–5% for next 3 days.
